claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a uniform FCC structure.
A metastable phase distribution is responsible for the baseline alloy's established toughness.
Nb content will be varied in increments of up to approximately ±5 at% relative to the baseline while processing is held constant.
Testing will be performed at temperatures up to approximately 700°C and at high strain rates.
Changing Nb content in CoCrFeMnNi modulates the stability of a metastable phase.
The metastable phase activates transformation-induced plasticity.
Nb-modified CoCrFeMnNi forms a metastable secondary phase such as B2.
The volume fraction and stability of the secondary phase modulate transformation-induced plasticity.
The volume fraction and stability of the secondary phase modulate crack bridging.
Variation in Nb content alters the phase-transformation threshold.
Variation in Nb content alters dislocation behavior.
An optimal Nb concentration increases energy dissipation through phase transformation and thereby enhances toughness.
Nb concentrations outside the optimal window cause a loss of toughness.
The optimal Nb content will produce higher fracture toughness than unmodified CoCrFeMnNi.
The optimal Nb content will produce greater strain hardening than unmodified CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold only within approximately ±5 at% Nb, up to approximately 700°C, and at high strain rates.
The toughness improvement and optimal Nb threshold may depend on composition, processing history, and other alloying elements.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as uniformly FCC while also having a metastable phase distribution, and the proposed mediator is a secondary phase such as B2. The relationship between a uniform single-phase baseline and this asserted pre-existing or newly formed secondary phase is not resolved.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy contains no Nb, so reducing its Nb content by as much as 5 at% or applying a ±5 at% Nb adjustment relative to that baseline is compositionally impossible.
